items.title: design(id): server-side invariants — budgets, observability, exploit resistance, containment
items.body: Fixes #5962 Design record for the #5955 worlds program child #5962 (statements S24–S27 of the 2026-11-04 brief). Docs only; no runtime limits, capability defaults, or policy values change. ## What it settles - **Budget set B1–B7** (§3), each with scope, accounting window, and one primary enforcement class out of **hard refusal / hard termination / throttle / bill**: per-call gas (B1), per-function per-tick fuel (B2), per-world per-tick aggregate (B3), per-session cumulative use (B4), per-world aggregate logical memory (B5), disk/storage per world (B6), library/module cache (B7). Landed numbers cite their constant and file; unsettled numbers are marked TBD with the owning research (#5966 mechanism, #6001 burst/tick calibration, #6002 timeout, #5965 compile/cache economics) and upstream anchors (wasmtime fuel/StoreLimits, Linux rlimits) instead of invented values. - **Trip observability** (§4): one trip record (budget, class, stable reason code, scope, accounting, retry), and three audience projections per budget — world author, server admin, and the affected function user — with the fault attribution rule that world-budget exhaustion is explicitly *not* the user's fault (no strike). - **Attack-surface checklist** (§5): the guest execution surface (import-free link, export allowlist, fuel/memory/message discipline, poison containment, snapshot fidelity, native rlimits) and a row for **all 20 registered providers** with the concrete bound each one already has, plus the file/network opt-in tier kept **off by default and first-party-only** pending the capability-control testing gate. - **Containment** (§6): why per-instance fuel/memory domains, atomic local refusals, and restore-time enforcement keep one world's exhaustion from degrading co-resident worlds; three shared-fate assumptions (A1–A3) and four open questions (O1–O4) stated explicitly. - **Reconciliation** (§2, E1–E12): the landed sandbox/world bounds checked against `pkgs/id/src/sandbox.rs`, `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_limits.rs`, `pkgs/id/src/world/core.rs`, `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs`, `pkgs/id/src/world/mod.rs`, `world_native.rs`, `world_compile.rs`. ## Scope discipline Consumes #7625's per-user mapping, failure table, and fuel-style fairness without re-deciding any of it; treats the #557 logical-memory ledger as a partial baseline (restore seam only, not disk or full runtime allocation); defers registry/prompt and capability-fact design to #5958/#6017 and compile-cache cost assumptions to #5965. Indexed in `doc/README.md` and `planning/architecture/README.md`. ## Verification Doc-only. Every named limit was cross-checked against the cited source file; provider count and default-ceiling membership were generated from `CATALOG_ENTRIES` (20 providers: 14 host + 6 platform modules; 2 excluded-by-default sensor caps). Upstream links fetch 200. No tests run: no code changed. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(id): discovery rejects apps whose program.source does not exist (#4064)
items.body: Fixes #4064 ## What `discover_apps` in `pkgs/id/src/app_manifest.rs` now checks a parsed manifest against its folder: when `[program].source` is declared, `folder.join(source)` must exist (file or directory). A missing source produces a named per-app error in `AppDiscovery.errors` — `: program.source does not exist in app folder ` — and the app is excluded from `AppDiscovery.apps`. Previously discovery registered any app whose `app.toml` parsed: `parse_app_manifest` validates only the source path's shape, and `discover_apps` statted only `app.toml` itself. Confirmed on main `070f0d99` by triage task 5962 — the pre-existing discovery test even registered an app whose `program/` directory was never created. ## Scope notes - `module_hash`-only manifests are unaffected (no source declared, no check). - Existing-file sources and existing-directory sources (tic-tac-toe's `program/`) both pass: the check is `Path::exists`. - No hashing/loading of the module at discovery; `resources.files` existence is not checked (pack-step question), per the issue's scope. ## Tests - New: `discovery_rejects_app_whose_program_source_is_missing` — ghost folder yields 0 apps and 1 error naming `program.source`, the declared path, and the missing existence. - Updated: `discovery_reports_bad_app_and_keeps_valid_app` fixture now creates the valid app's `program/` directory so its expectation survives the new check. - Targeted run on the laptop: `cargo test -p id --lib app_manifest` (results in the task 5972 completion note on #4064). items.title: doc(id): per-user function mapping design
items.body: Fixes #5967 Design record for the #5955 worlds program child #5967 (statements S46, S48–S51), produced under queue task 12870 (lane code-x, direct execution lane). ## What it settles (the acceptance criteria of #5967) - **Interface:** init/step entry points; state is an opaque, size-capped blob owned by the binding and stored verbatim by the world; the world offers a read-only view per tick; conformance checked once at bind/switch time. - **Per-tick mapping + failure table:** freeze → deterministic rotating order → metered invocation → exactly one outcome per binding → atomic state commit → tick log. The failure table covers success, fuel exhaustion, timeout, crash, malformed intent, oversized state, contract violation, world-budget exhaustion, suspension (3-strike default), and the impossible mid-tick unbind. - **Switching/trigger model:** switches are rebinds (#5964) effective only at tick boundaries; immediate vs next-load triggers differ by pre-emption/notification, never by breaking the boundary; conditional selection lives in a user-owned metered selector or an opted-in world trigger, with an explicit ownership split; conformance validated at request time. - **Human+AI-partner composition:** one binding, one budget, one intent; authority order human override → partner proposal → world default; blending mechanics stay with #5968. - **Fairness:** fuel-style budgets per the C4 interpretation recorded on #5967 (never wall-clock cross-host), per-function caps plus a world per-tick budget with a deterministic rotating start so budget cuts cannot permanently starve the tail; per-binding metering per F10; deterministic replay fit for the F8 adjudication substrate. Inputs cited: #5955, #5964, #5968, #5966, #5962, #5988 (states re-verified fresh 2026-11-08; #5988 is closed and its research doc is cited). Indexed in doc/README.md. Docs only; no code changes. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: doc: cooperative timeout contract for #6002
items.body: Contract specification for #6002: cooperative timeout — invocation budget, checkpoint convention, hard-kill outcomes. Queue task 13794 (lane code-g, direct execution per #8187). ## What this is One new file, `doc/2026-11-10_design_id6002_cooperative_timeout_contract.md`, plus its index line in `doc/README.md`. No code, no implementation. ## The contract in brief - **C1 — Invocation:** every invocation carries a budget bundle (fuel budget as the bound; an optional wall-clock deadline only in the cooperative single-host profile; tick identity; the binding's resume checkpoint). Self-observation (`fuel_used()` / `time_remaining()`) is contractual — the Screeps property the issue cites. - **C2 — Checkpoints:** function-initiated, host-mediated saves of function-local progress (opaque blob + host-assigned sequence + host-stamped fuel spent). A checkpoint is **not** a commit, never extends the budget, and survives exactly one kill as the next invocation's resume input. - **C3 — Hard kill:** exactly the #5967 failure-table row — default intent, pre-tick state (no commit), strike +1 — plus an outcome record `{binding, tick, kind, fuel_spent, checkpoint_offered}`. Partial results are discarded; the checkpoint is the only survivor, as input, not effect. - **C4 — Repeat offenders:** the #5967 strike discipline (consecutive, reset on success, suspension at the world limit, default 3), with outcome records queryable by the world author and a suspension event visible to author and user alike. ## Alignment Written against the landed #5967 mapping design (its failure table is adopted verbatim, not re-decided) and the #5966 research (Wasmtime fuel per binding as the primary bound). Enforcement mechanism, fuel costs, and budget numbers are explicitly left to their owning seams (#5966, #6001, #5962) — the spec names the seam wherever it needs a number those issues have not fixed. Refs #6002 (the issue stays open until this contract is merged, per its acceptance). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: design(id): two-level metering — burst bucket + hard per-tick ceiling, per function (#6001)
items.body: Closes #6001. The two-level metering design the mapping design (#5967) can implement against: - **Screeps mapped term-by-term** (§2): CPU limit → per-binding `refill`, bucket → capped per-binding fuel balance, burst draw → bucket draw bounded separately by a hard `tick_ceiling`, `Game.cpu.getUsed()` → the self-observation reads, per-account → per-function with the world ceiling composing above both levels. - **Accounting shape** (§3): credit/debit algorithm in mapping order — credit on tick boundaries only, world admission before bucket admission, store fuel set to `min(tick_ceiling, bucket_balance, world_remaining)`, actual consumption (incl. host charges, one currency) debited, full state reproducible from the tick log. - **Self-observation API** (§4): `getUsed()` / `getBucket()` / `getCeiling()` with honest-read semantics (exact at charge points, constant published charge, never outcome-changing) — the primitive #6002's cooperative contract and userland schedulers build on. - **Configuration** (§5): all three parameters are world-author config under server caps stated as relations; numeric defaults are TBD pending #5966 §6 calibration — no policy numbers invented. - **One new outcome row** (§7): `bucket-exhausted` as a throttle (skip, no strike), distinct from the fuel-exhausted hard termination. - **Holes hunted** (§8: function splitting, churn/idle farming, ceiling laundering, replay divergence) and **invariants with named oracles** (§9), per the C4 pillar doctrine on #5966. Docs only; no code. Indexed in `doc/README.md` and `planning/architecture/README.md`, following the #5962 record's pattern (PR #7977). ### Tokio broadcast channel calls clone in parallel, but does not require `Sync`
[GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The broadcast channel internally calls `clone` on the stored value when receiving it, and only requires `T:Send`. This means that using the broadcast channel with values that are `Send` but not `Sync` can trigger unsoundness if the `clone` implementation makes use of the value being `!Sync`.

Thank you to Austin Bonander for finding and reporting this issue.

#### Severity
